key_insight: The paper shows that inner GKP analog information can guide an adaptive policy that safely skips some outer surface-code syndrome measurements without increasing logical error.
engineering_relevance: This can cut measurement, ancilla, and circuit overhead in fault-tolerant quantum hardware, especially when syndrome-extraction noise is a major error source.
method: Use analog reliability from inner GKP correction to decide whether to measure or reuse syndromes.
At each round, choose among four actions: measure both Z and X stabilizers, measure only one type, or skip both and reuse previous results.
Compare the reliability of fresh noisy extraction against syndrome reuse for adaptive scheduling.
evidence_signal: Circuit-level simulations reported lower or comparable logical error rates to the full-measurement baseline while reducing the number of surface-code stabilizer measurements.
watch_item: The approach depends on accurate reliability estimates and may be less beneficial when idle noise dominates or when hardware cannot reliably provide the analog information used for decisions.
paper_title: When to Skip Syndrome Extraction in Surface-GKP Codes
